exposure: receiving treatment for anxiety or depression during pregnancy
outcome: physical symptoms (fatigue, nausea and vomiting, stomach cramping and abdominal pain)
prepregnancy conditions (endometriosis, hypertension, eating disorder, heart disease)
complications from past pregnancies (high blood pressure, preeclampsia)
delivery outcomes (mode of delivery, epidural use, stillbirth, miscarriage rates)
postpartum mental health (mental health composite scores, risk for perinatal mood disorder)
cohort: Participants were pregnant individuals who collected data in a decentralized digital trial using the PowerMom platform, divided into those reporting treatment for anxiety or depression (n=571) and those not receiving treatment (n=1505).
finding: Pregnant individuals reporting treatment for anxiety or depression experienced more physical symptoms and worse postpartum mental health outcomes than untreated individuals.
mod_finding: No significant differences were observed in mode of delivery, epidural use, stillbirth, and miscarriage rates between the two cohorts.
